## In one sentence

A reliable machine-learning project moves from a defined decision to validated,
reproducible predictions and monitoring.

## A minimal workflow

1. Define the decision, population, outcome, and time of prediction.
2. Inspect data quality, missingness, leakage, and sampling.
3. Create a reproducible train-validation-test split.
4. Establish a simple baseline.
5. Fit and tune models using training data and validation only.
6. Evaluate on the untouched test set and document limitations.
7. Monitor performance and data drift after deployment.

## Reproducibility

Record data versions, feature definitions, preprocessing, random seeds, model
settings, metrics, and software environments. A notebook is useful for
exploration, but reusable code and tests make the workflow dependable.

::: {.callout-tip}
The hardest part is often defining the target without using information that
would be unavailable at prediction time. Write the prediction timestamp down.
:::

## Check your understanding

Audit a proposed model for leakage. List one feature that might be unavailable
at prediction time and one monitoring signal you would track after deployment.
